village: The day the sun went out, the whole fishing village froze like stone statues. Only Grandma's lantern still flickered in Lam's hand.
Lam remembers Grandma calling every evening: "Lam, come home for dinner!" Now there is only the sound of the waves.
Grandma said: "This little flame holds everyone's memories. Don't let it go out." Lam gripped the lantern and ran.
bamboo: The bamboo forest creaks as if whispering old lullabies.
A letter slips from Lam's bag — the last letter Lam never got to deliver.
The Mist hides among the bamboo. It isn't evil; it only hungers for what has been forgotten.
terraces: The rice terraces once glowed gold at harvest. Now there is only the grey of the mist.
Lam finds a memory of a fresh meal — kitchen smoke, laughter, the smell of warm rice.
A scarecrow stands in the field like a guardian. Lam bows softly and moves on.
city: The city is abandoned; the streetlights died long ago. The roar of motorbikes lives only in memory.
On a fallen sign, Lam reads the name of the noodle shop Dad used to take them to.
The higher Lam climbs, the heavier the flame becomes. It carries the memories of so many people.
mountain: Dawn Mountain towers ahead. At its peak is where the sun used to sleep.
Lam understands: to relight the sun, something must be given away.
The Mist waits at the summit. Lam takes a deep breath.
